speaker: Doctor
text: The bruising is indeed spontaneous, and there is no abdominal or joint swelling noted. The night pain and spontaneous bruising are highly suggestive of bone marrow infiltration; I will await the results of the blood work, but if the smear confirms blasts or abnormal cells, I suspect leukemia. Did you notice any petechiae (tiny red spots) on her skin or any bleeding from her gums?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Unremarkable past medical history. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one younger sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history is unremarkable, which helps rule out prior congenital issues. To confirm my suspicion of acute leukemia, I need to see the blood results and look for specific signs of bone involvement. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, Peripheral Smear, and Coagulation Profile. REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray of long bones (femur/tibia) to check for lytic lesions.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL). The combination of bone marrow findings showing predominantly immature cells positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT, along with anemia, thrombocytopenia, and leukocytosis, confirms this diagnosis. Given the presence of fever and leg pain, I recommend evaluating for central nervous system involvement with a Lumbar Puncture and checking for organ infiltration with an Abdominal Ultrasound.
